body:
# the contributor audit: all-k deterministic-negative fractional gamma bound


`candidate 93a759825a881af9`.
The precise proved conclusion is G_(k,p)>9/20 for every integer k>=1
and every real p in[0,1]. It is an auxiliary probability theorem.

the contributor read the whole proof and executable, rederived the exact probability
formula, and reran the integer/rational certificate. Output: PASS for
363 mesh enclosures, 71 finite gamma bounds, seven extended tail entries,
and every infinite-range cutoff and interpolation gap.

## Analytic range and interpolation

For k>=3, the zero-extended gamma density has continuous derivative and
integrable differentiated transform. Fourier inversion bounds its
derivative by (1/(2pi))*2/(k-2). Convolution with a probability density
cannot increase that norm. The Taylor remainder of the survival function
is therefore bounded globally by y^2/[6(k-2)]. The centered perturbation
p(E-1) has variance p^2, so the displayed expectation inequality follows
without a tail cutoff or an unbounded remainder.

The integration-by-parts identity follows from (xe^(-x))'=(1-x)e^(-x).
Its boundary terms vanish for the bounded density functions used here.
It gives G'(p)=-p times the derivative of the density after addition of
p Gamma(2), and hence the stated global Lipschitz constants. The k=1
Laplace density is globally Lipschitz; its isolated nondifferentiability
is harmless under the integration. For k=2, the negative-halfline bound
is 1/4, and the only positive-halfline secondary extremum has size
2e^(-3/2)/4<1/4. Endpoint continuity is justified by the independent
negative exponential and the absence of an equality atom.

The integer-gamma comparison A_m>1/2 follows by strictly comparing the
two density values at m+s and m-s and retaining the tail beyond2m.
The removed geometric sum is strictly below q_m. Jensen for log on
each unit interval proves the factorial bound with the correct direction.
The elementary estimates e>8/3 and e<87/32 have explicit series proofs.
At k=83 the positive rational number 233/4860 may legitimately be
squared; its squared margin over 3/(16*82) is positive. Both error terms
decrease thereafter, covering every larger k. All 71 smaller gamma
certificates include the previously absent m=75,...,81 indices.

## Exact probability enclosures

For W=Gamma(k)-Exp, direct convolution gives

    f_W(w)=e^w/2^k for w<0,
    f_W(w)=e^(-w) sum_(j=0)^(k-1) w^j/[j!2^(k-j)] for w>=0.

Integrating the latter expression gives the source's survival
e^(-s)Q_k(s). Conditioning on W at s=k-1+p gives

    Pr(W+pE>=s)=S_W(s)+e^(-s/p) int_(-infinity)^s e^(w/p)f_W(w)dw.

The negative integral is p/[2^k(1+p)]. Integration by parts of each
nonnegative monomial term on[0,s] gives exactly the displayed F_j,C_j
recurrences. Thus the two-exponential formula is independently derived
from the actual density. The endpoints p=0 and p=1 use the correct
gamma shapes and thresholds, rather than evaluating a singular formula.

Taylor degrees32 and33 bracket exp(-r) on[0,1], including r=1. Pairing
the terms after degree3 proves positivity of the lower bound. Raising
positive endpoints to an integer power and multiplying preserves the
enclosure. Signed coefficients are handled by reversing interval
endpoints, so large cancellation near p=1 cannot invalidate a lower
bound. The exact rational program checks the inequalities themselves;
its small interval-width check is only diagnostic.

The 33 mesh points are endpoints of32 equal intervals. Every real p is
within1/64 of one of them. Combining this distance with the proved
constants1/2,1/4,and at most1/3 yields losses1/128,1/256,and1/192.
All three displayed final gaps above9/20 are exact positive fractions.
There is therefore no interpolation or large-parameter range left
uncertified, and no premise that a minimum occurs at a mesh point.

## Consequence for the separately proved reduction

The dimension-free escape implication audited in
`historical context (not an accepted premise)` now applies with c=9/20.
It gives probability>=9/20 for every finite capped balanced coefficient
vector with one fixed negative unit. Together with the audited exact
minima in dimensions3,...,9, it proves the capped simplex angular
surplus >=(7/6)(d/(d+1))^d for all d>=3. This still supplies no
reduction from arbitrary mixed-integer convex bodies to that family.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
